paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus goes to the people who know they need Him. He walks up to Levi at the tax booth, the one window in town where nobody walks up smiling, and says, "Follow Me." Then He sits down at Levi's table with tax collectors and sinners. When the scribes who were Pharisees grumble about it, Jesus says, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick." (Mark 2:14-17)

So what does that mean for you, baker? It means you don't have to clean yourself up before you come to Him. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer and I did NOT have my act together, and He still reached in and called me out. The only thing He asks is that you come as you are and follow.

Then Jesus gives the bridegroom picture, the old garment and the old wineskins, and they all say one thing: Jesus is the new thing God is doing. Something this new won't be stitched onto the old routines like a patch. It needs room to work. He says, "Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins." (Mark 2:22) So stay close to Him, because the wedding guests are with the bridegroom. And the story isn't over, friend, so keep listening.
